Content:
Let [MATH: n] be a positive integer. The set [MATH: \mathbb{Z}_n] of residue (or equivalence) classes modulo [MATH: n] is called the integers modulo [MATH: \boldsymbol n{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{ [\, 0 \,]_n\,, [\, 1 \,]_n\,, [\, 2 \,]_n\,, \quad \ldots, \quad [\, n-1 \,]_n \big\}.]

Content:
It's normal to drop the [MATH: n] subscript from the residue classes when the modulus is clear. So, we can also write

Content:
[MATH: \mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{ [\, 0 \,], [\, 1 \,], [\, 2 \,], \quad \ldots, \quad [\, n-1 \,] \big\}.]

Content:
The set of integers modulo [MATH: n] is special because we can perform arithmetic with its elements.

Content:
- The addition of "integers" (classes) in [MATH: \mathbb Z_n] is defined as
[MATH: \big[ \, a \, \big] + \big[ \, b \, \big] = \big[ \, a+b \, \big].]
For example, in [MATH: \mathbb Z_4,] we have
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] + [\, 3 \,] = [\, 2+3 \,] = [\, 5 \,].]
Recall that we can pick any element of a residue class as its representative. Since [MATH: [\, 5 \,] = [\, 1 \,]] because [MATH: 5\equiv 1\, (\textrm{mod} \: 4),] we can write our answer as
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] + [\, 3 \,] = [\, 1 \,].]
- The subtraction of integers in [MATH: \mathbb Z_n] is defined as
[MATH: \big[ \, a \, \big] - \big[ \, b \, \big] = \big[ \, a-b \, \big].]
For example, in [MATH: \mathbb Z_4,] we have
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] - [\, 3 \,] = [\, 2-3 \,] = [\, -1 \,].]
Since [MATH: [\, -1 \,] = [\, 3 \,]] we can write our answer as
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] - [\, 3 \,] = [\, 3 \,].]

Content:
In other words, we add (or subtract) integers modulo [MATH: n] as usual and compute the residue modulo [MATH: n] at the end.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Let [MATH: n] be a positive integer. The set [MATH: \mathbb{Z}_n] of residue (or equivalence) classes modulo [MATH: n] is called the integers modulo [MATH: \boldsymbol n{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{ [\, 0 \,]_n\,, [\, 1 \,]_n\,, [\, 2 \,]_n\,, \quad \ldots, \quad [\, n-1 \,]_n \big\}.]

Content:
It's normal to drop the [MATH: n] subscript from the residue classes when the modulus is clear. So, we can also write

Content:
[MATH: \mathbb{Z}_n = \big\{ [\, 0 \,], [\, 1 \,], [\, 2 \,], \quad \ldots, \quad [\, n-1 \,] \big\}.]

Content:
The set of integers modulo [MATH: n] is special because we can perform arithmetic with its elements.

Content:
- The addition of "integers" (classes) in [MATH: \mathbb Z_n] is defined as
[MATH: \big[ \, a \, \big] + \big[ \, b \, \big] = \big[ \, a+b \, \big].]
For example, in [MATH: \mathbb Z_4,] we have
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] + [\, 3 \,] = [\, 2+3 \,] = [\, 5 \,].]
Recall that we can pick any element of a residue class as its representative. Since [MATH: [\, 5 \,] = [\, 1 \,]] because [MATH: 5\equiv 1\, (\textrm{mod} \: 4),] we can write our answer as
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] + [\, 3 \,] = [\, 1 \,].]
- The subtraction of integers in [MATH: \mathbb Z_n] is defined as
[MATH: \big[ \, a \, \big] - \big[ \, b \, \big] = \big[ \, a-b \, \big].]
For example, in [MATH: \mathbb Z_4,] we have
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] - [\, 3 \,] = [\, 2-3 \,] = [\, -1 \,].]
Since [MATH: [\, -1 \,] = [\, 3 \,]] we can write our answer as
[MATH: [\, 2 \,] - [\, 3 \,] = [\, 3 \,].]

Content:
In other words, we add (or subtract) integers modulo [MATH: n] as usual and compute the residue modulo [MATH: n] at the end.

Content:
The complete addition table modulo [MATH: 4] is shown below.

Content:
